messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for service/text-gen -> prod-canary-4. Image: registry.redwood/internal/text-gen:2026-03-15-canary. Link: https://deploys.redwood/team/deploys/9876 :rocket:

pagerduty: INCIDENT #INC-4921: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (canary). Pager: eng-oncall -> paging Alice M. :rotating_light:

Alice M.: oncall here, seeing spike in 500s from canary hosts 10.4.2.14/15. Alerting graph: https://grafana.redwood/d/abc123/canary-errors :eyes:

Bob K.: I can repro a curl to canary returning 502 consistently. Next step: check pods/images.

Bob K.: `kubectl -n prod describe pod text-gen-canary-6d7f4` -> Image: `registry.redwood/internal/text-gen:staging-2026-03-10` — that looks wrong, should be canary build tag `2026-03-15-canary` :confused:

Carol (SRE): who rolled that canary? deploy link shows pipeline id 7842. Checking CI artifacts...

Carol (SRE): CI logs (snippet):
```
[2026-03-15T13:06:01Z] restored layer from cache key: docker-layer-abc123
[2026-03-15T13:06:02Z] Found cached artifact for /app/bin -> using cached binary from previous build
[2026-03-15T13:06:05Z] Tagging image as registry.redwood/internal/text-gen:2026-03-10
```
That explains it — cache hit pulled older binary and tag step picked wrong metadata. Possible cache poisoning of build cache.

Alice M.: ok immediate mitigation: kill the canary feature flag and pause rollout.

Alice M.: `curl -X POST "https://launchdarkly.redwood/api/flags/redwood_canary_v2/off" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LD_TOKEN"` -> toggled to OFF :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Feature flag redwood_canary_v2 set to OFF by Alice M.

Bob K.: Rolling back canary to stable image now. Command: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/text-gen --to-revision=41`

deploy-bot: Rollout undo started for deployment/text-gen -> targetRevision=41. Monitoring health checks...

Carol (SRE): Observability: errors on /v1/generate dropping back to baseline within 2 minutes of rollback. Metrics: https://grafana.redwood/d/abc123/canary-errors?from=now-15m :thumbsup:

Eve L.: re: root cause, did published artifact metadata come from a shared cache bucket? Looks like the cache key didn't include the build SHA, so two different pipelines could pick up artifacts. Filed infra ticket: INFRA-1298 (CI cache key hardening).

Alice M.: Good catch. For immediate follow-ups: 1) Block redeploys until CI cachefix (guard in pipeline), 2) Add tag-check in deploy step to verify image digest matches expected SHA, 3) Postmortem plan. Assigning to Eve L. and Carol (SRE).

Eve L.: I'll own the pipeline fix. Starting a PR to change cache key to include commit SHA + pipeline id, and adding a guard that fails deploy if tag digest != expected. Will provide ETA in the ticket.

Bob K.: small note for ops: we should add an alert for mismatched image tags between rollout metadata and actual pod image (simple check). I'll open a monitoring PR.

Alice M.: TL;DR for handoff -> incident contained, customer impact limited to canary traffic only, rollback successful, workaround (flag off) applied. Next on-call please watch for any regressions over the next 2 hours.

Carol (SRE): adding follow-up actions to ticket and assigning postmortem.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-4921 updated: status=contained, severity=SEV2, assignees=[Eve L., Carol (SRE)]. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-4921

Alice M.: handing off to next oncall @Bob K. — short summary above. If anything pops, page me. :coffee:

Bob K.: taking over. Monitoring cluster and CI artifacts channel. :eyes:
